{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. {"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

blocks.text:
call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Wait — I notice a latent shell bug in the pkill shim: `--[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*` skip-case: `-TERM` → `[A-Z]*` → continue ✓. BUT `-fT`-style MIXED bundles: body `fT` — first char lowercase → not `[A-Z]*` → scanned → 'T' not c/v → pass to pgrep → pgrep rejects → rc2 → exec real ✓ fine.

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

Now — a REAL bug I want to double check in the shim: the skip-case `[Ss][Ii][Gg]*` — body `stop`?? "stop" → s,t,o,p: [Ss]✓ [Ii]? 't' ✗ → not skipped → scan: s,t,o,p — no c/v → sel → pgrep -stop → reject → rc2 → real pkill: `pkill -stop` → pkill -s top?? -s = session id selection taking an argument... weird but honest-real ✓ fine.

`--signal=KILL` in the ENTRY scan: body `-signal=KILL`... starts with '-' → `-[a-zA-Z]*` matches (first char '-'? NO — the token is `--signal=KILL`: `case "$a" in -[a-zA-Z]*)` — '-' then '[a-zA-Z]' must match the SECOND char which is '-' → NO match ✓ skipped (it goes through the main peel loop ✓).

`--signal=CV`? second char '-' → entry-scan skipped ✓; main loop: `--signal=*` → sig='CV' → kill CV pid → kill error → out stays 0 → exit 1 — real pkill would error too ✓ fine.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

The killall shim has a subtle bug: `pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" -x "$n" 2>/dev/null) || continue` — pgrep rc=1 (no match) → continue ✓; rc=2 (bad flag — impossible here) ✓. But pgrep -x on a name with no match → rc 1 → continue ✓ good.

One issue: `for n in $names` — killall receives names joined with SPACES (`names="$names $1"`) — names with SPACES break; killall names are comm names (no spaces in practice) — acceptable, and killall names come as separate argv anyway.

Now — one more REAL bug candidate in the pkill shim: `self=$` — the SHIM's pid. But pgrep -f "<pattern>" ALSO lists the SHIM itself (its cmdline contains the pattern!). Excluded via self ✓. But ALSO lists the `sh -c` that RAN the shim?? The shim is invoked directly (exec from PATH lookup by the wrapper shell) — the wrapper `sh` stays alive as the PARENT (it waits for the shim) — parent excluded ✓. And pgrep itself — procps pgrep excludes itself ✓.

BUT — WAIT: one more subtlety in the pkill shim: the `kill` in the shim is a dash builtin — `kill "$sig" "$p"` — sig like `-9` ✓.

What about `pkill -f pattern` matching the DART VM **which is the parent of everything** — protected via env ✓. And the test-runner's `dart` JIT subprocesses (frontend servers)? NOT protected → killed ✓ desired (E2).

Alright — the code review is done. Now — I want to also double-check `_probeOwnProcessGroup` probe and `boot sweep` / `processGroupTableSnapshot` style probes that READ ps tables for JOB GROUPS (issue #517 boot sweep): the boot sweep recognizes a job's leftover GROUP by pgid — unaffected by argv shape ✓.

And the shell_jobs boot reconcile `processTableSnapshot` (pid,lstart) — matches job pids ✓ unaffected.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Wait — I notice a latent shell bug in the pkill shim: `--[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*` skip-case: `-TERM` → `[A-Z]*` → continue ✓. BUT `-fT`-style MIXED bundles: body `fT` — first char lowercase → not `[A-Z]*` → scanned → 'T' not c/v → pass to pgrep → pgrep rejects → rc2 → exec real ✓ fine.

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

Now — a REAL bug I want to double check in the shim: the skip-case `[Ss][Ii][Gg]*` — body `stop`?? "stop" → s,t,o,p: [Ss]✓ [Ii]? 't' ✗ → not skipped → scan: s,t,o,p — no c/v → sel → pgrep -stop → reject → rc2 → real pkill: `pkill -stop` → pkill -s top?? -s = session id selection taking an argument... weird but honest-real ✓ fine.

`--signal=KILL` in the ENTRY scan: body `-signal=KILL`... starts with '-' → `-[a-zA-Z]*` matches (first char '-'? NO — the token is `--signal=KILL`: `case "$a" in -[a-zA-Z]*)` — '-' then '[a-zA-Z]' must match the SECOND char which is '-' → NO match ✓ skipped (it goes through the main peel loop ✓).

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;

done

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. #!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

Now — a REAL bug I want to double check in the shim: the skip-case `[Ss][Ii][Gg]*` — body `stop`?? "stop" → s,t,o,p: [Ss]✓ [Ii]? 't' ✗ → not skipped → scan: s,t,o,p — no c/v → sel → pgrep -stop → reject → rc2 → real pkill: `pkill -stop` → pkill -s top?? -s = session id selection taking an argument... weird but honest-real ✓ fine.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:

    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do

    -[a-zA-Z]*)

      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;

      fa_rest="$fa_body"

        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

't' ✗ → not skipped → scan: s,t,o,p — no c/v → sel → pgrep -stop → reject → rc2 → real pkill: `pkill -stop` → pkill -s top?? -s = session id selection taking an argument... weird but honest-real ✓ fine.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

/// The `pkill` PATH shim: expands the match with the REAL `pgrep` (the
/// same selection engine and flags), filters the protected pids, the
/// invoking shell (`PPID`) and the shim itself, then signals the rest with
/// the requested signal (default `SIGTERM`). Selection shapes the shim
/// does not model (signal after the pattern, `-u root`, `-t tty`, `-n`,
/// `-o`, …) exec the real `pkill` — honest behavior over silent guessing.
String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
    r'''#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --signal) sig="${2-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    -[0-9]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
    -*) sel="$sel $1"; shift ;;
    *) break ;;
  esac
done
# Exactly one operand (the pattern) must remain; anything else — unknown
# flags interleaved with it, extra operands — is the real pkill's call.
if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
  exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
fi

# The selection flags ride along: pgrep shares pkill's selection engine.
pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@" 2>/dev/null)
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then
  # pgrep rejected the selection (a flag it does not share): the real
  # pkill decides, semantics stay honest.
  exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
fi
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
# pgrep -l rows are "pid name" — keep the pid column.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A `bash` tool command containing a broad kill (`pkill -f`, `killall`, `kill`) matched its own `setsid sh -c '<command>'` wrapper — the raw script rode the wrapper argv, so `/proc/<sh_pid>/cmdline` contained every literal substring of the script (`sh-167` died `exit -15`). The same broad `pkill -f "dart "` also matched the `fa` harness itself (JIT `dart` cmdline) and SIGTERMed it; `_gracefulHeadlessExit` then printed the generic `aborted: Operation aborted` + `exit 130`, aborting the leg mid-run without `outputs/response.md`.

### Fix

- **Wrapper argv isolation** (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`): POSIX scripts are written to a per-exec private temp dir and run as `sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — the wrapper argv never carries the script body. A guard prelude restores `sh -c` parity (`set --`; `$0` stays `sh`); exit codes, `set -e`, `pwd`, heredocs and `stdin`/`liveStdin` forwarding are unchanged. Legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery remains the fallback if the temp dir cannot be created. Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- **Harness/ancestor pid immunity** (new `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`): a once-per-process provision injects `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` (harness pid + ancestor chain up to init + process group) and puts `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims first; a `kill()` prelude function filters `kill` arguments. Protected pids and the invoking shell are never signaled; legitimate victims (stuck test runners, background servers) still die (edge case E2). Unsupported selection shapes (`-u`, `-t`, `-c`, `-v`, …) exec the real binary.
- **Signal provenance** (`bin/fah_util.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`): headless `SIGTERM` now logs `fa: SIGTERM received — aborting headless run gracefully` before the abort. Exit code contract unchanged (130 graceful, 143 on the second SIGTERM).

### Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` — 13 tests: `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 via foreground, background job, and the `bash` tool (pre-fix: `exit -15`); `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; protected pid skipped by `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` while an unprotected match is reaped; `$0`/`$#`/exit-code/`set -e`/heredoc/cwd parity. All RED before the fix, all GREEN after.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` — the SIGTERM mid-turn test now also asserts the abort names `SIGTERM` on stderr.
- Full suite: 2755 tests passed, 0 failures (`dart test`, includes the tagged integration/pty legs); `dart analyze` clean.

### Notes

- `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is visible to scripts (`echo`/`env`) by design — it is a defense boundary, not a secret.
- The guard intentionally covers the harness chain and the job's own shell only; `kill -9 -1`-style deliberate attacks and absolute-path `/usr/bin/pkill` invocations stay outside the shim's reach.
- One pinned test updated deliberately: `an explicit env PATH is preserved, not replaced` now asserts the caller's PATH survives *behind* the guard shim dir instead of being `/bin` first.

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='/usr/bin/pkill'
FA_REAL_PGREP='/usr/bin/pgrep'

sig=''
sel=''
# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    -[a-zA-Z]*)
      fa_body="${a#-}"
      case "$fa_body" in
        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
      esac
      fa_rest="$fa_body"
      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
        case "$fa_c" in
          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
        esac
        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
      done
      ;;
  esac
done

Another one — THE `-x` flag bundles `-xf`: chars x,f — neither c/v → sel → pgrep -xf ✓ good.

Now — a REAL bug I want to double check in the shim: the skip-case `[Ss][Ii][Gg]*` — body `stop`?? "stop" → s,t,o,p: [Ss]✓ [Ii]? 't' ✗ → not skipped → scan: s,t,o,p — no c/v → sel → pgrep -stop → reject → rc2 → real pkill: `pkill -stop` → pkill -s top?? -s = session id selection taking an argument... weird but honest-real ✓ fine.

`--signal=KILL` in the ENTRY scan: body `-signal=KILL`... starts with '-' → `-[a-zA-Z]*` matches (first char '-'? NO — the token is `--signal=KILL`: `case "$a" in -[a-zA-Z]*)` — '-' then '[a-zA-Z]' must match the SECOND char which is '-' → NO match ✓ skipped (it goes through the main peel loop ✓).

/// The `pkill` PATH shim: expands the match with the REAL `pgrep` (the
/// same selection engine and flags), filters the protected pids, the
/// invoking shell (`PPID`) and the shim itself, then signals the rest with
/// the requested signal (default `SIGTERM`). Selection shapes the shim
/// does not model (signal after the pattern, `-u root`, `-t tty`, `-n`,
/// `-o`, …) exec the real `pkill` — honest behavior over silent guessing.
String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
    r'''#!/bin/sh
# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
set -u
FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
