{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

Now — while waiting, poll periodically. Let me also double check there are no leaked fa_sh_cmd_ dirs even after crashes... 0 ✓.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.

blocks.text:
The suite is actively running tests that spawn `bin/fah.dart` (PID 30843 — a PTY/integration leg). 65% CPU on the runner, healthy progress.

Interesting side observations:
1. `ls /tmp | grep -c fa_sh_cmd_` = 0 — no leaked per-exec temp dirs ✓ (cleanup works; also none leaking from the suite's hundreds of bash calls ✓).
2. `fa_sh_guard_` = 43 dirs — one per PROCESS that provisioned the guard (the suite spawns MANY fa processes — each provisions once → 43 dirs). This confirms the per-process leak of the shim dir. 43 tiny dirs from one suite run — for a LONG-lived fa each leaks ONE dir; acceptable but 43/run shows it accumulates across process restarts with no reaper. Hmm — the OS won't reap /tmp automatically (systemd-tmpfiles cleans by age on many distros). For long-running dev machines this could accumulate thousands over weeks? Each dir = 2 tiny files (~2KB). A dev machine restarting fa hundreds of times a day → ~500 dirs/day → ~180k/year — untidy but bounded-ish; tmpfiles reapers usually handle it. 

Could I reduce it? Options: (a) reuse a WELL-KNOWN per-user dir (e.g. /tmp/fa_sh_guard_<uid>) instead of createTemp — same path reused across processes, shims are content-identical except baked real paths (same host → same) — but two fa processes with DIFFERENT protected pids — the pids come via ENV not the shim files ✓ shims are pid-independent! So a shared per-uid shim dir works: write-if-missing (atomic rename), never delete. Race-safe via rename. That removes the leak entirely.

Hmm — but a stale dir from an OLD version of the code (renamed shim format) would persist and PATH-shadow with stale shims!! Version-stamp the dir name (fa_sh_guard_<uid>_<shimHash>)? The hash changes when the builder changes → new dir, old ones still leak. Cleanup: on provision, opportunistically delete OTHER fa_sh_guard_<uid>_* dirs? Race: another fa process mid-exec using the old dir → deleting shims under it → PATH lookup fails → bash tool errors?! deleteSync of a file being EXECUTED is fine on POSIX (the running shim keeps its inode; new lookups fail while a call is mid-flight — the exec happens per lookup: `pkill` PATH lookup during a script = if file gone → "not found" → command fails (exit 127) — degrades a pkill call to an error — BAD for a concurrent process.

Trade-off: one leaked dir per fa process launch vs cross-process delete races. The ticket doesn't demand /tmp hygiene; the pragmatic v1 = accept the leak, note it in the code comment (already noted: "a leaked temp dir is reaped by the OS" — that comment is for per-exec script dirs which DON'T leak (0 on disk ✓); the guard dir leaks per process). Let me at least DOCUMENT it accurately in the code. Actually — improvement worth the complexity? A simple, race-safe improvement: name the dir deterministically per-boot: `fa_sh_guard_<pid-of-fa>` — still leaks per process. No.

Simplest real fix: a per-process SHARED dir under the FAH session root? Sessions live under ~/.fah — the guard is env-level (lib), no access to session paths there. /tmp it is.

Decision: accept + document (the honest comment). 43 dirs ≈ 86KB per CI run — negligible for CI; dev machines get tmpfile reaping. Note it in response.md Notes.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — bash tool: `pkill -f` self-matches its own `sh -c` wrapper

## Root Cause

Every POSIX `bash` tool call runs as `sh -c '<entire command>'`, so the full
script body sits in the wrapper's own argv/cmdline. Any `pkill -f <pattern>`
inside the command matches that cmdline first and kills its own shell before
the real target (observed: `sleep 30` survived, the call died with exit -15).
The same self-exposure extends to the harness: a harness-side `fa` process
matching the pattern, or the invoking tool shell, can be caught by broad
`pkill`/`killall`/`kill` sweeps.

## Fix

- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): provisioned once per process —
  a private temp dir with PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` and a `kill()`
  shell function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; legitimate
  victims keep matching. Provision failure degrades to today's behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts now delivered from a
  per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — restores
  `$0`/`$#` positional-param parity, so exit codes, `set -e`, heredocs and
  stdin behave identically) so the wrapper argv never carries the script
  body; guard dir + `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` merged into each exec env; headless
  `SIGTERM` aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (exit contract
  unchanged: 130 graceful / 143 escalate). Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log line on the
  headless run/serve paths.
- `AGENTS.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`: documented the delivery + guard contract.

## Test Coverage

- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13 tests): `pkill -f <unique>;
  echo survived` exits 0 with `survived` through `LocalShell.exec`,
  `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool itself (all RED pre-fix: exit -15);
  `pgrep -f` no longer lists the wrapper; a pid on `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS` is
  skipped by the shim/`kill()` while an unprotected process matching the
  same pattern is still reaped; script-file parity (`$0`, `$#`, exit codes,
  `set -e`).
- `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`: PATH assertion updated — the guard
  shim dir leads, the caller's PATH survives behind it.
- `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart`: headless SIGTERM abort now
  also asserts the `SIGTERM` name appears on stderr.
- Focused suites (env / bash tool / shell jobs): 310 passed, 0 failed.
  Full default suite (the CI `test-core` gate): see final run below —
  0 failures. `dart analyze` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- Guard is opt-out-safe: any provision failure (unwritable tmp, odd
  namespace) silently falls back to the legacy `sh -c <command>` delivery.
- The per-process shim dir is intentionally not deleted at exit (a
  concurrent process may be mid-lookup); cost is one ~2 KB dir per fa
  process launch, bounded by OS tmp reapers.
- Full-suite verification: the in-flight run at 20:48 covered all code;
  one doc-comment-only edit landed during the run, so the suite was
  re-run against the final tree afterwards — both runs green.
