{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

blocks.text:
**CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

Hmm, but actually WAIT: is FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE in the test's env? The spawned fa inherits the TEST RUNER's env = my bash tool env = fa agent env (has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE? The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

That explains:
- yolo tests: session answered via real LM instead of scripted → no 'removed'.
- backend_mode boot stalls: sessions tried the REAL provider (network latency/rate limits under load) instead of the scripted local one... or the scripted holder never got the request because the session used the real queue first. `--attach`/`--output events` timeouts: same env-leak stalls.
- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

ALL of it: my agent's own env (FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE / FA_LOG_FILE etc.) leaks into `dart test` child processes. PRE-EXISTING infra flakiness of running the suite from inside an fa session — NOT my code change. 

Can I prove it cleanly? Re-run the 4 failing integration files with the leaking vars UNSET (env -i or explicit unset FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE FA_LOG_FILE ...) on the quiet box. If green → environmental proof, on the CURRENT tree, close to done.

Which vars? From the output: FA_LOG_FILE, FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE. Maybe also FA_SESSION-ish vars. I'll unset a targeted list: FA_LOG_FILE FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE FA_PROVIDERS FA_PROVIDER FA_SESSION FAH_* etc. Let me check my own env for FA_*/FAH_* keys first. Then run the 4 files + the composer/yolo/log files (7 files total) with them scrubed.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 14): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity (`$0`, exit codes, `set -e`).
- Full default suite: +12021 ~62, 0 product regressions (see Notes). `dart analyze` clean; CRAP diff gate OK; providers suite green in isolation.

### Notes
- The only suite failures are pre-existing environment limits, reproduced identically on the pre-fix tree via `git worktree` at d4b4428: `test/browser_ext/` (Chrome service worker can't start, no DBus on the runner — that dir owns its own `browser-ext.yml` workflow) and load-flaky provider watchdog tests (green in isolation on a quiet box).

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

blocks.text:
**CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

Hmm, but actually WAIT: is FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE in the test's env? The spawned fa inherits the TEST RUNER's env = my bash tool env = fa agent env (has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE? The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

That explains:
- yolo tests: session answered via real LM instead of scripted → no 'removed'.
- backend_mode boot stalls: sessions tried the REAL provider (network latency/rate limits under load) instead of the scripted local one... or the scripted holder never got the request because the session used the real queue first. `--attach`/`--output events` timeouts: same env-leak stalls.
- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

ALL of it: my agent's own env (FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE / FA_LOG_FILE etc.) leaks into `dart test` child processes. PRE-EXISTING infra flakiness of running the suite from inside an fa session — NOT my code change.

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider...

I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? **CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

**CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

Hmm, but actually WAIT: is FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE in the test's env? The spawned fa inherits the TEST RUNER's env = my bash tool env = fa agent env (has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE? The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

That explains:
- yolo tests: session answered via real LM instead of scripted → no 'removed'.
- backend_mode boot stalls: sessions tried the REAL provider (network latency/rate limits under load) instead of the scripted local one... or the scripted holder never got the request because the session used the real queue first. `--attach`/`--output events` timeouts: same env-leak stalls.
- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

ALL of it: my agent's own env (FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE / FA_LOG_FILE etc.) leaks into `dart test` child processes. PRE-EXISTING infra flakiness of running the suite from inside an fa session — NOT my code change.

**CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

Hmm, but actually WAIT: is FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE in the test's env? The spawned fa inherits the TEST RUNER's env = my bash tool env = fa agent env (has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE? The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

That explains:
- yolo tests: session answered via real LM instead of scripted → no 'removed'.
- backend_mode boot stalls: sessions tried the REAL provider (network latency/rate limits under load) instead of the scripted local one... or the scripted holder never got the request because the session used the real queue first. `--attach`/`--output events` timeouts: same env-leak stalls.
- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

ALL of it: my agent's own env (FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE / FA_LOG_FILE etc.) leaks into `dart test` child processes. PRE-EXISTING infra flakiness of running the suite from inside an fa session — NOT my code change.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response...

# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response...

I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? {"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

All deliverables in place, tree clean, everything committed. Final summary:

## gh-1763 — complete

**Bug**: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a `bash` tool command matched its own `sh -c '<command>'` wrapper argv and killed its own shell (exit -15) before the real target.

**Fix** (3 layers, root-cause only):
1. **Script delivery** — POSIX commands now run from a per-exec private temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` with a `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude), so the wrapper argv never carries the script body and can't self-match.
2. **Bash guard** (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`, new) — provisioned-once PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude excluding the harness pid chain (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`), process group, and invoking shell; real victims still match; any provision failure degrades to the old behavior.
3. **SIGTERM forensics** — headless aborts now log `fa: SIGTERM received …` so a child-issued kill can't masquerade as Ctrl+C (130/143 contract unchanged).

**Verification**: RED → GREEN TDD (repro test committed before the fix, `git` history provable), 13/13 self-defense tests green, `+11961 ~62` full suite with **zero failures attributable to the change** — all 17 failures reproduced and attributed by controlled experiment (5 = Chrome/DBus env, 11 = dev-agent `FA_*` env leaking into spawned sessions, 1 = pre-existing PTY render flake proven failing 3/3 on the pre-fix tree).

**CRITICAL FINDING**: The yolo rm test failure is NOT a timeout — it's a REAL behavioral difference:

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider... 

NO WAIT. Reread: the test spawns `fa` with env carrying the scripted provider URL. The actual reply came from a REAL greeting — "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? That's an ENV-LEAK test-isolation bug in the harness tests themselves (pre-existing), triggered when the runner env has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE set — MY OWN session (fa agent on this box) exports it!

Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

Hmm, but actually WAIT: is FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE in the test's env? The spawned fa inherits the TEST RUNER's env = my bash tool env = fa agent env (has FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE? The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

- yolo tests: session answered via real LM instead of scripted → no 'removed'.
- backend_mode boot stalls: sessions tried the REAL provider (network latency/rate limits under load) instead of the scripted local one... or the scripted holder never got the request because the session used the real queue first. `--attach`/`--output events` timeouts: same env-leak stalls.
- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

ALL of it: my agent's own env (FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE / FA_LOG_FILE etc.) leaks into `dart test` child processes. PRE-EXISTING infra flakiness of running the suite from inside an fa session — NOT my code change.

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response... 

Hold on — `Running build hooks...Running build hooks...` INSIDE the actual output — the session's own bash exec printed "Running build hooks..." TWICE — that's the DART BUILD HOOK message (native assets build hooks) that appears when dart runs... in MY OUTPUT TOO (my dart test runs printed "Running build hooks...Running build hooks..." repeatedly!). This message pollutes stdout of anything dart-runs on this box. It's in the SESSION's PTY output.

And crucialy: `"source":"reported"` token line — the session talked to a REAL provider?? "glm-5.3-flash"!!! The session used the REAL glm provider — NOT the scripted one! `note: provider queue (2 entries) from FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE env — the queue is the main model` — FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE from the ENVIRONMENT (the runner has fa configured globally — MY OWN SESSION's env!) leaked into the spawned test session, which then used the REAL LM (glm-5.3-flash) instead of the test's scripted provider...

I'm Fa, ready to help with coding tasks in /tmp/yolo_rm_ws_DJHSDA" — that's a REAL LM response (glm-5.3-flash, input 1620 tokens). The spawned session PREFERRED the env's FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (inherited from MY AGENT'S ENVIRONMENT) over the test's --provider? Is that pre-existing? YES — nothing to do with my change. It's caused by running the suite INSIDE an fa agent session whose env leaks into child processes. Same class for the boot stalls? Different mechanism but same "environment pollution" family.

The note says "from the FA_LOG_FILE env var" for the trace — yes, the runner env is MY agent's env: .dmtools/fa-trace.log is MY session's trace!). So the spawned sessions inherit MY agent's fa configuration — REAL provider queue — and the tests that don't EXPLICITLY override the provider talk to the real glm!!!

- headless_log_file / headless_tools_flag: sessions reached the REAL provider → real (slow) responses → timeouts/parsing misses.

{"content":"# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

The test drives a headless fa session with a scripted provider, asks it to run `rm -f /tmp/...`, and expects the transcript to contain 'removed' (the rm tool output). Actual output: the model said "Hi! I'm Fa..." — the SESSION responded to a greeting?? No wait — look at the actual: `The user just said "hi". This is a trivial greeting turn...` — that's a THINKING line! And `fa-tokens ... "input":1620` — the session made ONE request and replied "Hi! I'm Fa, ready to help".

The test uses a SCRIPTED provider (a fake LM returning canned tool-call responses). The session made its request, and instead of executing the rm, the session's FIRST turn answered "Hi!" — meaning the SCRIPTED RESPONSE didn't line up... OR the session counted the boot/system request differently.

Wait — "input:1620, requests:1" and the reply is a greeting to "hi" — the test's scripted provider probably: turn 1 → tool_call(rm), turn 2 → "done". The session instead showed a greeting response...
